bases.unresolved_premise: No dated, detailed SAP or protocol section is captured that establishes when the complete analysis plan was finalized relative to access to unblinded outcome data.
bases.stopping_rationale: The registry's primary-outcome entry was posted before the reported primary completion date, and the article identifies the endpoint as prespecified and describes its primary model. Searches and inspection of the full captured supplement and registry did not locate a dated detailed analysis plan or unblinded-access date.

answers.justification: The registry record specifies daily self-diary average pain intensity on a 0–10 scale for up to six months and was first posted in 2010, before the study's 2014 primary completion. The article calls the primary endpoint prespecified and reports the corresponding 24-week repeated-measures model. This supports probable prospective specification, though the captured Sources do not establish a dated full SAP or exact timing of unblinded access.
unknowns: The date the complete analysis plan was finalized and the date investigators/statisticians first had access to unblinded outcome data are not reported.

answers.justification: The registry's primary measure is average pain intensity from the participant's daily numerical-scale diary through six months, which corresponds to the reported weekly mean pain-intensity change over 24 weeks. The report labels this as the primary outcome and presents other pain dimensions and pain-intensity summaries as secondary outcomes. There is no indication that this primary measurement was selected because its results were favorable.
unknowns: A detailed dated protocol listing every eligible pain-intensity measure is unavailable, so the full prespecified measurement set cannot be verified.

answers.justification: The report identifies a repeated-measures mixed model for the prespecified primary endpoint, and the supplement reports the post-hoc results under LOCF, interpolation, maximum-likelihood, and MCMC multiple-imputation methods rather than withholding those alternative missing-data analyses. The available reports give no reason to believe the primary adjusted estimate was selected from analyses on the basis of its results.
unknowns: The detailed analysis plan and all analyses eligible under it are not available, so a results-driven choice among any unreported model specifications cannot be ruled out completely.

interpretation: Corroborates eligible-space reasoning, not a gold label or demonstrated error. Frozen original untouched.

bases.stopping_rationale: I read the dated protocol/SAP front matter, the original protocol outcome and timing, the SAP outcome and analysis sections, and the report’s data-collection and analysis passages. These do not report investigator access to unblinded results, so chronology cannot be determined.

answers.justification: The original protocol (version 5, 27 November 2015) specified pain intensity at six weeks post-intervention; given the 12-week intervention, this corresponds to 18 weeks after randomization. The SAP specifies the approved NRS endpoint at 18 weeks post-randomization and the report collected the last primary endpoint on 28 November 2019. However, the SAP front matter says it was drafted on 2 March 2020, and the sources do not say when investigators gained access to unblinded outcomes or whether the final analysis intentions were fixed earlier. The timing criterion therefore cannot be determined.
unknowns: When investigators first accessed unblinded outcome data; whether analysis intentions were finalized before that access.

answers.justification: The protocol lists pain intensity on the NRS as a primary outcome at six weeks post-intervention, corresponding to 18 weeks post-randomization. The report presents pain intensity at 18, 26, and 52 weeks, so the listed eligible time points are reported. The captured protocol does not identify alternative pain scales or definitions from which the 18-week estimate appears to have been selectively reported.

bases.unresolved_premise: The captured record does not establish the complete set of eligible analysis alternatives finalized before investigators could access unblinded outcomes.
bases.stopping_rationale: I inspected the SAP analysis section and the report’s statistical analysis section. They describe the primary mixed-effects analysis and reported estimate, but do not establish the complete pre-unblinding set of eligible alternatives; the SAP is dated after the last primary endpoint collection and access timing is unavailable.

answers.justification: The SAP specifies a mixed-effects model for the primary outcome and a coefficient estimating the 18-week between-group effect; the report uses a linear mixed model and reports the time-specific mean difference. The sources do not establish whether other eligible analysis choices were considered and selectively withheld, or whether the SAP was finalized before access to unblinded outcomes. Multiplicity alone does not show results-driven selection, so this remains no information.
unknowns: Whether alternative eligible models or analysis choices existed and were selectively withheld based on results; when analysis intentions were finalized relative to unblinded access.
